clue.text: Kind of cheese for a sad mood?

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a vein is a mood or tone, as in 'in a lighter vein'

explanation.surface: Someone asks which cheese suits a melancholy frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-veined cheeses such as Stilton are a recognised type of cheese marbled with mould.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: a stud is a raised knob or ornament, like a shield's centre
the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: The man who runs a horse-breeding farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is both a decorative knob on a surface and the person who manages others.

clue.text: British diplomats in America they're out of this world!

indicators.note: in puts the diplomats inside the letters for America

parts.note: US is the United States, America
FO is the Foreign Office, home of British diplomats

explanation.surface: British envoys posted to the States are out of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are popularly thought to be alien craft from beyond Earth.

clue.text: Vicars ordered to welcome the first lady opposite

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other
ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters of Vicars are shuffled

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Clergy are told to greet the President's wife, who sits across from them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' scrambles the clergy word, and 'to welcome' takes the first lady inside it; 'the first lady' is Adam's partner in Genesis, not a president's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the other way round, with the order reversed.

clue.text: Ricer boiling madly is now beyond redemption

indicators.note: madly says the letters of the two words are mixed wildly

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget heating up wildly is now hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrigible means incapable of being reformed or corrected, past saving.

clue.text: Term of modification braved somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of braved come out in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A word for change has been faced up to in some fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this part of speech modifies a verb, adjective or another such word.

clue.text: Heading off internal rising showing some tension

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
heading off means the first letter is cut from the word

parts.note: inward means internal or inner

explanation.surface: Removing the top of something on the inside shows it is a little strained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' drops I from INWARD, leaving NWARD; 'rising' turns that over.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tense and tired, showing strain.

clue.text: More painting required in college department

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective naming a kind of university department, for courses outside the college walls

parts.note: extra means more
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A college department needs more artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An extramural department teaches students outside the university proper, literally beyond its walls.

clue.text: Comedy hero shortage during British summer

indicators.note: during means the shortage comes within the other pieces

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder
lack means a shortage

explanation.surface: A comedy character endures a shortfall over the British summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who adds up figures. Blackadder is the cunning antihero of a BBC sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Blackadder is the title character of the BBC historical comedy series.

clue.text: Old copper used in standard valve

indicators.note: used in places the old copper inside the word for standard

parts.note: stock means standard, as in a stock reply
PC, police constable, is a British copper

explanation.surface: An antique copper part is fitted to an ordinary valve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal, but it is the policeman, PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a tap or valve controlling the flow in a water pipe.

clue.text: Chanted words reduced danger to trespassers

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the trap word is lost

parts.note: a mantrap is a trap set for intruders on private land

explanation.surface: Words sung out are a lesser threat to those who trespass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly in meditation or prayer.

clue.text: I sit by lake — such grandeur!

parts.note: I sit (for an artist) can be put as I'm posing
Ness is the Scottish loch, a lake

explanation.surface: An artist's model sits beside a lake and marvels at the splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sit' must be read as I'M POSING, as a model sits for a portrait; Loch Ness is a lake in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposingness is the quality of being impressive and stately, that is grandeur.

clue.text: Morality play to uplift all of us

parts.note: Everyman is the famous medieval English morality play
to jack up is to lift something

explanation.surface: A medieval morality play is meant to raise everyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplift' sounds moral, but it only means to raise, as a car jack does.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for every single person without exception.

clue.text: Constriction of nerve on part of body

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
the neck is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A medical note about a pinched nerve on part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point that restricts flow, a constriction.

clue.text: Scene actor played, giving cause to be respected

indicators.note: played means acted out loosely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's scene, once performed, gives reason for respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make sacred, so causing something to be revered.

clue.text: Oxygen has obstinate pervasive quality

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
dour can mean stern and obstinate

explanation.surface: Oxygen is said to have a stubborn, all-pervading character.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell or aura is a quality that pervades a place or a thing.

clue.text: Press sure to be inflexible

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: The press is certain to be unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironbound means rigid and unyielding, literally bound with iron.

clue.text: Berlin's air conducive to original thought?

definitions.meaning: Irving Berlin wrote the popular song of this title
blue-sky thinking is unconstrained, creative thought

explanation.surface: The atmosphere in the German capital encourages fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' is not the city but the songwriter Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is both an Irving Berlin song and the clear open space behind blue-sky thinking.

clue.text: Conductor taking opera to province repeatedly

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: repeatedly means the province's abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A conductor keeps taking an opera on tour round the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the Province' is Northern Ireland, NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: American maturity custom

parts.note: age means maturity, as in coming of age

explanation.surface: A list of three nouns about American grown-up habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice or habit, the same as custom.

clue.text: Entertainer whose fans await his forthcoming release?

definitions.text: Entertainer whose fans await his forthcoming release?

parts.words: Entertainer whose fans await his forthcoming release?
parts.note: sounds like a pop star with a new record due, but the release is from chains, locks or a tank

explanation.surface: A performer's followers eagerly await his next record.
explanation.definitionFit: Houdini-style performers free themselves from restraints, so the audience literally awaits their release.

clue.text: Lawmen have final vessel removed

indicators.note: removed means the vessel's letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: to possess is to have
SS, steamship, is a vessel, taken from the word's end

explanation.surface: Police officers must have the last boat taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Get smaller cart, say

indicators.note: say indicates that the word for cart is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon or cart

explanation.surface: A request to make the cart a bit smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to decrease or dwindle, like the moon.

clue.text: Clothing son in check

indicators.note: in places the son abbreviation within the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check

explanation.surface: A boy's outfit is being inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is an undergarment or waistcoat, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Pass out with start of ill-health's return

indicators.note: out with the start means the first letter is thrown away

parts.note: a relapse is the return of an illness

explanation.surface: Someone faints as an illness first comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting, but 'Pass' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Muse needs a little time inside to intervene helpfully

indicators.note: inside places the small time abbreviation within the word for intervening

parts.note: to mediate is to step in to settle a dispute
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice that a thoughtful person needs a short time indoors to help sort things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think deeply, a synonym of meditating.

clue.text: It's sharper for one lamenting

definitions.meaning: more keen, so sharper or more acute
to keen is to wail for the dead, so one who does it laments

explanation.surface: A mourner is the sharper one.
explanation.definitionFit: Keener is both the comparative of keen and a noun for a professional mourner.

clue.text: For me, easiest to travel about one

indicators.note: about means going round the letter standing for one
to travel sets the letters of easiest moving into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone states that, personally, the simplest way to travel is round one place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges the letters of the superlative, and 'about' wraps that scramble round I (one), so the surface's journey is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in my opinion, giving one's own personal view.
